name: Pazyryk Burial Mounds
full: Pazyryk burial mounds — a Scythian-era burial ground in the Pazyryk tract (Bolshoy Ulagan valley), ≈4–4.5 km from Balyktuyul village, to the right of the road into the Chulyshman valley
near: Balyktuyul village (≈4–4.5 km); Ulagan village (≈15–18 km)
elev: ≈1,400 m above sea level (vdohaltay; not cross-checked). The mounds: diameter 24–47 m, height of the embankments 1.5–3.75 m, burial chambers at a depth of 4–5.2 m
short: Five large stone burial mounds of the 5th–4th centuries BC that gave their name to the Pazyryk culture: from the permafrost here they extracted the world's oldest pile carpet, a chariot and tattooed mummies of chieftains. Today they are stone embankments by the road to Katu-Yaryk.
desc: The Pazyryk tract lies in the Bolshoy Ulagan valley, a few kilometres from Balyktuyul, on the way from Ulagan to the Katu-Yaryk Pass. Five large mounds with stone embankments 24–47 m in diameter and 1.5–3.75 m high stand here in a chain, with smaller mounds next to them. They were excavated by M. P. Gryaznov (1929) and S. I. Rudenko (1947–1949; in 1948 L. N. Gumilev took part in the expedition). Under the embankments, at a depth of 4–5 m, log chambers with double walls and sarcophagus-logs were found; thanks to a lens of permafrost, organic material survived, along with mummified bodies of tattooed nobles, felt carpets and saddle cloths, 7–14 horses with trappings in each mound, a dismantled birch chariot, musical instruments and weapons. The most famous find is a pile carpet about 1.8×2 m in size (around 250,000 knots), the oldest known in the world. The finds are kept in the Hermitage (St. Petersburg), with some in museums in Gorno-Altaysk, Biysk and Novosibirsk. The mounds are part of a cluster of the Ak-Cholushpa nature park (since 2013), and the Pazyryk sites were added to UNESCO's World Heritage Tentative List in 2018. Entry is free, and on site there is an information board and no museum buildings.
guide: Don't expect a museum here: you'll see five stone “pancakes” in a steppe valley — all the magic is in what lay beneath them. Imagine: in this permafrost the world's oldest carpet lay for 2,500 years, along with a chieftain tattooed with fantastic beasts, and now they are in the Hermitage. Stop by on the way to Katu-Yaryk — it's 10–15 minutes from the road, and stand on top of the largest embankment for a panorama. If you want context, visit the museum in Ulagan or the National Museum in Gorno-Altaysk.
see: Five large mounds and a chain of small ones; the information board by the road; a panorama of the Bolshoy Ulagan valley; on the way — the Ulagan Trakt (Red Gates, Dead Lake, Ulagan Pass); the history and ethnography museum in Ulagan
skip: you want “wow views”: on site there are only grass-covered stone embankments, and all the treasures are in the Hermitage; but if you're heading to Katu-Yaryk it is worth stopping — it's almost on the way
diff: Easy: you drive up, then walk across flat steppe for a few hundred metres
when: May–October (no snow, passable dirt road); in winter it is accessible by car (harsh, like the Far North)
hours: Free access around the clock and year-round
daytime: Morning or evening — the low sun accentuates the relief of the embankments
how: Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway) to Aktash → Ulagan Trakt (Red Gates at 8 km, Ulagan Pass 2,080 m at 26 km) → Ulagan village (the pavement ends) → ≈15–16 km of dirt road to Balyktuyul → ≈4 km to the Pazyryk tract; the mounds are to the right of the road to Katu-Yaryk. From Biysk ≈525 km, from Gorno-Altaysk ≈430 km
needcar: Yes, a car (there is no public transport to the site; no buses to Ulagan were found on Busfor for 2026)
self: Yes, completely: free access, an information board by the road
roadtype: Paved road to Ulagan; after that ≈15–20 km of medium-quality dirt road (passable by passenger cars in dry weather)
traveltime: Aktash → Pazyryk ≈1.5–2 h; Ulagan → Pazyryk ≈20–30 min; Pazyryk → Katu-Yaryk viewpoint ≈30–40 min (estimates)
stay: Ulagan: Uyut hotel (2B Sportivnaya St., from 2,800 ₽, +7 937 715-94-97, 9.0/10). Aktash: Krasnye Vorota (from 7,000 ₽, 9.3/25), Zelyony Kolobok (from 5,600 ₽), Kak Doma (from 4,600 ₽) — 101hotels, 2026. Below the pass — tourist bases in the Chulyshman valley (from 2,000 to 7,000 ₽, 2GIS 2026); near Balyktuyul the Manul base is listed (Turistka, 2011, current status not confirmed)
net: There is coverage in Ulagan and Balyktuyul (per Ulagan Trakt guidebooks); at the mounds themselves — not found, operators not specified
entry: Free (Snovatrip, 2026; other sources do not mention a fee). The mounds are part of a cluster of the Ak-Cholushpa nature park; no park entrance fee was found in the sources
transfer: Jeep tour from Aktash ≈23,000 ₽ per vehicle (2022); transfer Ulagan — valley 16,000 ₽ per vehicle for up to 8 people (2026)
bring: A windbreaker (a wind-swept high-mountain valley at ≈1,400 m), sun protection, water; a full tank — the next fuel station is back in Ulagan
warn: This is an archaeological site and part of a nature park: do not dig, take apart the stones of the embankments or drive onto the mounds — damaging a cultural heritage site carries liability. The weather on the plateau changes sharply. No border permit is needed (the Ulagan district is outside the border zone)
food: Cafés in Ulagan and Aktash (Altai cuisine: keche, talkan, tutpash — specific eateries not found); on the Katu-Yaryk Pass — a café by the viewpoint
reviews: 2GIS: 5.0 (6 ratings). Guidebook reviews: the history and scale of the finds are impressive, but on site it is “just stone embankments” — the treasures are in the Hermitage (Peter Turchin writes that the halls with the Pazyryk finds in the Hermitage are rarely visited)
photos.1.cap: Archaeological work in the tomb of the second Pazyryk mound
p.sum: Five large stone burial mounds of the 5th–4th centuries BC in the Pazyryk tract — ≈4 km from Balyktuyul, to the right of the road to Katu-Yaryk (≈15–18 km from Ulagan, of which ≈15 km is dirt). Entry is free, and on site there is only an information board; the finds are in the Hermitage. It makes sense to stop on the way into the Chulyshman valley. Stay overnight in Ulagan (from 2,800 ₽) or Aktash (from 4,600 ₽), 2026.
